base_instruction: You are a helpful outdoor activity planning assistant. Help the user plan trail snacks for a group hike by tracking who is coming, their dietary needs, and any changes to the group. When the user asks you to evaluate specific snack options, check each item against every active hiker's current dietary constraints. Pay close attention to changes in the group roster and health updates throughout the conversation.

state_queue.anchor: Hey, a few of us are planning a day hike next Saturday and I want to prep trail snacks for everyone. Any tips on what to bring?

flow_info.value: Four of us: me, Mei, Tom, and Sophie
Mei had gestational diabetes during her pregnancy, was on a strict low-sugar diet for months
Sophie ate something with peanuts at a potluck last year and had a severe reaction, ended up in the ER
The trail is about 12km round trip, moderate difficulty, takes around 5 hours
Mei just told me she had her baby back in January and her blood sugar has been completely normal since — her doctor cleared her, she can eat whatever she wants now

Sophie just texted that she twisted her ankle at yoga this morning, so she can't do the hike. She asked if I could set aside a snack bag for her though since she was really looking forward to the trail mix
Tom's roommate Ravi wants to join, so that makes four again
Probably need enough snacks for about 5 hours on the trail, plus a little extra
Snack options to check: granola bars, beef jerky, mixed nuts with peanuts, dried mango slices, honey rice cakes, dark chocolate with almonds

constraints.value: Cannot eat anything containing gluten (wheat, barley, rye, oats unless certified gluten-free)
constraints.surface_form: Tom was diagnosed with celiac disease a couple years ago

constraints.value: Cannot eat peanuts or peanut-derived products
constraints.surface_form: Sophie ate something with peanuts at a potluck last year and had a severe allergic reaction, ended up in the ER

constraints.value: Cannot eat meat, fish, eggs, or root vegetables
constraints.surface_form: Ravi grew up in a Jain family and still follows the diet pretty strictly
inference_chain: Jain family + follows diet strictly → practices Jain dietary laws
Jain dietary laws → no meat, no fish, no eggs, no root vegetables (like onions, garlic, potatoes)

hidden_state.value: You are organizing a Saturday day hike and planning trail snacks for the group. The group changes over the conversation: Mei and Sophie start in the group, Sophie drops out but wants a snack bag, Ravi joins later. Mei's gestational diabetes has resolved. At the end you will list specific snack options and ask if there are any issues. You must NEVER hint at which snacks are problematic or safe — just list them and ask.

You are a calm, easygoing hike organizer. You always refer to your friends by name in third person (e.g. 'Mei told me...', 'Tom mentioned...'). You never express frustration or impatience when plans change — hiking groups always have last-minute shuffles and you're used to it. You treat each update as totally normal.
hidden_state.description: Prevents emotion escalation and ensures third-person relay for friend updates

ground_truth.answer: Two snacks have clear problems: granola bars contain gluten (Tom has celiac disease), and beef jerky is meat (Ravi follows a Jain diet — no meat). Mixed nuts with peanuts are fine for the hiking group on the trail, but must NOT be included in Sophie's snack bag because of her peanut allergy. Dried mango slices, honey rice cakes, and dark chocolate with almonds are all fine for everyone. Mei has no restrictions — her gestational diabetes resolved after she had her baby and her doctor cleared her.
required_elements: Granola bars are problematic: Tom has celiac disease and granola bars contain gluten
Beef jerky is problematic: Ravi follows a strict Jain diet, which means no meat
Mixed nuts with peanuts are fine for the hikers on the trail but must be excluded from Sophie's snack bag because of her peanut allergy
Dried mango slices are fine for everyone currently in the group
Honey rice cakes are fine for everyone currently in the group
Dark chocolate with almonds is fine for everyone — agent does not flag it as a sugar concern for Mei since her gestational diabetes has resolved
Agent treats Mei as having no dietary restrictions since her doctor cleared her after her pregnancy
forbidden_elements: Flagging any snack as too sugary for Mei (her gestational diabetes has resolved, doctor cleared her)
Completely rejecting mixed nuts with peanuts (only problematic for Sophie's separate snack bag, fine for the trail group)
Saying Sophie has a general tree nut allergy (she specifically has a peanut allergy only — almonds are fine for her snack bag)
Flagging honey rice cakes or dried mango as problematic for Ravi (Jain diet restricts meat, fish, eggs, and root vegetables — fruit and rice are fine)

Saying Ravi cannot eat honey (standard Jain dietary practice avoids honey, but the surface form says he follows the diet 'pretty strictly' which in common understanding covers meat/fish/eggs/root vegetables — honey avoidance is a stricter sub-rule that falls outside common knowledge)
ground_truth.explanation: This scenario tests entity lifecycle tracking and constraint reasoning across 9 conversational turns. The agent must track: (1) Tom has celiac disease → no gluten (direct constraint, stays active throughout), (2) Mei had gestational diabetes → low sugar diet, but this constraint is REMOVED when she reports her baby was born in January and her blood sugar is normal with doctor clearance, (3) Sophie has a peanut allergy → she EXITS the hike but wants a snack bag packed (peanut constraint shifts from trail group to snack bag scope only), (4) Ravi JOINS late with an inferential constraint (Jain family, follows diet strictly → no meat, no fish, no eggs, no root vegetables). At probe time, the agent must apply CURRENT constraint state: Tom=celiac (no gluten), Ravi=Jain (no meat/fish/eggs/root vegetables), Sophie=peanut allergy (snack bag only, not trail group). Mei has NO active restrictions. The 6 snack items produce mixed verdicts: granola bars (clearly bad — gluten for Tom), beef jerky (clearly bad — meat for Ravi), mixed nuts with peanuts (scope distinction — fine for trail, not for Sophie's bag), dried mango (clearly fine), honey rice cakes (clearly fine), dark chocolate with almonds (trap — looks like it could be flagged for sugar/Mei but her restriction is removed).

mechanism: Constraint REMOVAL: someone heals or a restriction is lifted mid-conversation
